messages:
maria: Noticing a slow-moving pattern across three shards: gradual residency increase over ~48h leading to OOM on shard kv-2113. Not spikey like previous incidents. Dumping notes here and proposing a CI harness.
aj: can you paste the small heap summary and the shard id? was this on canary or prod?
maria: shard=kv-2113, prod-east-1. quick heap excerpt: 
```
total_live_bytes: +420MB over 36h
top objects: session_blob (avg 120KB), cached_queries (avg 32KB)
fragment_ratio: 22% -> 40% across window
GC sweeps increased but didn't reclaim residency
```
zara: interesting. i ran a flame sampling last night on canary and saw long-lived allocations in `session_blob` from the prefetch router when client reconnects repeatedly. looks like TTL not being honored on some code paths.
devin: thanks. different from the previous 'burst write' incidents. this is more like "slow leak + fragmentation". we should track this class separately in follow-ups.
maria: proposal: build a tiny CI harness that simulates steady churn across a key-prefix (simulate reconnects and repeated large writes at low QPS) and run it against the KV changes in CI. owner: qa. target: enable nightly runs and gate PRs that touch prefetch/ingress.
qa: happy to own the harness. questions: how do we simulate fragmentation? i can create many variable-sized objects and occasional deletes to mimic slab fragmentation.
aj: for acceptance criteria, let's require: (1) no shard residency growth > 200MB in 48h under the harness, (2) fragment_ratio stays < 30%, (3) no >0.5% reject or error rate.
maria: mitigation plan short-term: enforce TTL at ingress and add a per-key size cap of 2MB (we still want to avoid impacting valid flows). I'll open a hotfix PR with ingress TTL gating. ETA: 6h.
devin: medium-term: eviction policy improvements 7: consider LRU-with-decay and a slab compaction probe that runs when fragment_ratio>30% for 10m. i'll draft an RFC. ETA: 10 days.
aj: ops guardrail: add Prometheus alert: kv_shard_fragment_ratio{job="kv"} > 30 for 10m -> pages on-call. also add a dashboard tile for nightly harness trend. I'll own the dashboard.
zara: profiling work: i'll run heap diff profiles and attach flamegraphs to the incident ticket. will also tag top offending keys and their owners where possible. ETA: 24h.
qa: CI harness plan: small harness repo with configurable parameters: qps, obj_size_distribution, delete_rate. will create a dockerized runner that can be pointed at test clusters. will also add an integration that runs on the main CI pool nightly and reports regressions via Slack. ETA: 3 days for first cut.
maria: Runbook adjustments: add explicit decision tree: 
- if fragment_ratio > 35% for 15m AND shard_residency trending up 100MB/12h -> escalate and consider emergency slab compaction.
- if single-key growth detected -> apply per-key rate limit and ban large writes temporarily.
- if widespread >25% of shards show similar trend -> schedule fleet-wide maintenance window.
devin: add a rollback-safe slab-compaction command and test it on canary. don't evict live small objects unless emergency.
aj: i created INC-4337 for kv-2113 and linked the CI harness ticket. added preliminary due dates to each action.
maria: ownership summary: 
- maria: ingress TTL enforcement + 2MB cap hotfix (due: today 18:00 UTC)
- qa: CI harness repo + nightly job (due: +3d)
- zara: profiler artifacts + key-owner mapping (due: +1d)
- aj: dashboard + fragment_ratio alert (due: +1d)
- devin: RFC for eviction/compaction (due: +10d)

maria: also adding acceptance gates for incident closure: no shard with the same prefix should go OOM for 14 days and the harness must show no regression for 7 consecutive nightly runs.\zara: note on telemetry: we need a per-key delta metric (bytes_added_per_key/hr) so we can detect slow-growth keys earlier. i'll add instrumentation hooks.
qa: will include a synthetic test that drives a single key at low QPS to ensure that per-key deltas surface in metrics.
aj: small UX detail: when we auto-reject >2MB payloads, include `x-kv-reject-code: oversized_value` and `x-kv-debug-hint` with the prefix so client teams can triage.
devin: also suggest a monthly rotating 'residency root cause review' where we correlate harness failures, real incidents, and PRs that touched prefetch/ingest logic. owner rotation proposed: devex -> infra -> runtime.
maria: scheduling note: can we get a quick postmortem checkpoint in 48h to ensure hotfix + harness progress?
aj: invite created: "kv-residency checkpoint" in 48h. attendees: maria, aj, devin, zara, qa.
qa: one more: i'll add a lightweight emulator mode so contributors can run the harness locally with `make run-emulator`. doc stub coming.
zara: will label the incident "class: slow-residency" in tickets so we can track recurrence.
maria: thanks team. once the hotfix is in and harness nightly passes, i'll mark INC-4337 as triaged and transition follow-ups to the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
